subject: Human Evolution
title: CT Scanning Fossils
description: A quick win: understand CT Scanning Fossils.

hook.text: Some fossils are too fragile or too valuable to cut open. CT scanners see inside without touching them.

buildup.text: High-resolution CT scans create 3D maps of internal structures: brain casts, ear bones, tooth roots.

discovery.text: Inner ear shape reveals how a species balanced—key evidence for whether it walked upright.

twist.text: Virtual fossils can be shared globally. Any lab can now study a rare skull without ever touching it.

climax.text: CT scanning turned fragile, irreplaceable specimens into infinitely shareable digital objects.

punchline.text: The best way to study a fossil is to never touch it.

quiz.question: What can inner ear CT scans reveal about a fossil species?
